text: Previous ratio=6.0 right boundary was cutting off an EMA500 high-response region. Extending ratio to 8.0 (SL in {4,5}, width 3-14, lookback 20-160) reveals a broad improvement region: aggregate mean cumulative net R climbs with ratio and peaks around ratio~7.5, then deteriorates at ratio=8.0. SL=4: r6.0=+51.5R, r6.5=+70.7R, r7.0=+79.6R, r7.5=+99.7R (median +104.5R, max +172R), r8.0=+88.2R. SL=5: r6.0=+73.0R, r6.5=+69.7R, r7.0=+86.7R, r7.5=+102.5R (median +103.5R, max +158R), r8.0=+82.5R. Both SL values independently show the same ratio topology (peak near 7.5, rollover at 8.0), which is stronger evidence of a genuine peak than either alone.

The new high-response region is structurally robust, not a single extreme cell. At SL=4/ratio=7.5, its structural core is approximately width 6-9 x lookback 50-80: mean cumulative net R by width is w3=+100.6R, w4=+129.0R, w5=+94.4R, w6=+132.3R, w7=+135.5R, w8=+142.0R (peak), w9=+123.6R, w10=+64.7R (n=15 cells per width, averaged over lookback 20-160); mean by lookback is lb20=+101R, lb30=+95R, lb40=+104R, lb50=+114R, lb60=+120R, lb70=+124R (peak), lb80=+112R, lb90=+102R, falling to ~+87R by lb100 and staying in the +81..+98R range through lb160. The global maximum observed cell is width=8, lookback=70, SL=4, ratio=7.5: +172R across 440 trades.

The improvement up to ratio~7.5 is supported by both trade directions, not a long-only artifact. At SL=4, the long/short decomposition tracks ratio: r6.0 = +35.3R long / +16.2R short, r6.5 = +45.2/+25.5, r7.0 = +44.3/+35.3, r7.5 = +51.0/+48.8 (near parity), r8.0 = +54.1/+34.1 -- the r7.5-to-8.0 aggregate rollover is driven by short deteriorating (+48.8R -> +34.1R) while long keeps improving (+51.0R -> +54.1R), which is evidence of a real peak in the short-side response rather than an artifact of the ratio range's endpoint. The structural-ridge cell width=8/SL=4/ratio=7.5 decomposes to +71.1R long / +70.9R short, near-exact side parity. The global max candidate (width=8, lookback=70, SL=4, ratio=7.5, +172R) itself has short (+93.5R) slightly exceeding long (+78.5R).

SL=6 does not continue the SL=4/SL=5 improvement pattern -- negative/limiting evidence for further stop widening beyond this line's already-tested range. Across ratio 6.0-8.0 (width 3-14, lookback 20-160), SL=6 aggregate mean cumulative net R is r6.0=+77.5R, r6.5=+79.1R, r7.0=+66.6R, r7.5=+80.0R, r8.0=+81.2R -- a positive but roughly flat/uneven plateau, materially below SL=4/5's ratio~7.5 peak (+99.7R/+102.5R), with no emerging next-step improvement as ratio increases.

The EMA500 surface may contain two distinct useful exit regimes for the same structural (width/lookback) setup, rather than one regime with a single tunable TP: a symmetric-exit ridge around 4 ATR/4 ATR (width 7-8, lower lookback), and a separately strong asymmetric-continuation regime around SL 4-5 ATR x ratio~7.5 (TP roughly 30-37.5 ATR) at width 6-9 x lookback 50-80. This is a hypothesis about regime structure, not a finding -- it has not been tested against the intermediate ratio range or validated as distinct from a single continuous response surface.

refs.note: это hypothesis, не finding и не decision — требует отдельной проверки; предложенный следующий шаг (по мнению ревьюера) — не расширять сетку further, а сначала внимательно разобрать устойчивость локальной поверхности вокруг SL4-5/ratio7-8/width6-9/lookback50-80 (N, соседние клетки), прежде чем решать про новый расчёт
